clue.text: Thanks to the powerful one for what we have received?

parts.note: ta is an informal British word for thanks
a king is the mighty figure on the throne

explanation.surface: Sounds like grace before a meal, with thanks offered to the Almighty.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes the grace 'For what we are about to receive...'; the 'powerful one' is a monarch, not God.
explanation.definitionFit: Takings are money received by a business, so a taking is something received.

clue.text: Fierce creature concerning foolish man when rearing

indicators.note: in a down clue, rearing means rising up, so the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: re means concerning, about
git is British slang for a stupid man

explanation.surface: A beast that rears up against a foolish man.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiger is a big cat famed as a fierce predator.

clue.text: With bits of kitchen vegetable stuck to metal drawers they complain

indicators.note: only small bits, the first letters, of the words kitchen and vegetable are used

parts.note: etchers draw images by biting lines into metal plates

explanation.surface: Someone moans about bits of vegetable stuck to the metal kitchen drawers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawers' suggests furniture, but here it means people who draw.
explanation.definitionFit: To kvetch is Yiddish-derived slang for whingeing, so kvetchers are habitual moaners.

clue.text: How to record e.g. dance movement? Thanks for putting in the idea

definitions.text: How to record e.g. dance movement?

indicators.note: the word for thanks is put into the word for idea

parts.note: a notion is an idea
ta is an informal British word for thanks

explanation.surface: Someone thanks another for planting an idea about recording dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Dance notation, such as Labanotation, is a written system for recording choreography.

clue.text: Horse that's wild in a rocky place

parts.note: a mount is a horse for riding

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters of in a running out of order

explanation.surface: A wild horse roams a rocky landscape.
explanation.definitionFit: A mountain is a high mass of rock, a natural rocky place.

clue.text: Seaweed and gull waste university's taken away to make aromatic ingredient

parts.note: ore is an old word for seaweed (as in oreweed)

indicators.note: the letter U for university is removed

parts.note: guano is the droppings of seabirds such as gulls

explanation.surface: A grim recipe combining seaweed and bird droppings into a flavouring.
explanation.definitionFit: This herb of the marjoram family is a fragrant seasoning in cooking.

clue.text: One's leader is spiked; two editors required

indicators.note: to spike a story is to kill it, so the first letter of one is dropped

parts.note: the word one, with 's standing for is

indicators.note: two signals that the abbreviation is used twice

parts.note: ed is the short form of editor

explanation.surface: Newsroom talk: the lead story was spiked, so two editors are needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Needed and required are synonyms meaning wanted as necessary.

clue.text: Hamlet produced by Almeida with no hint of Moriarty. I'll go with that

indicators.note: the remaining letters are produced in a new order
the letters named are removed from Almeida
only the first letter of Moriarty is the hint

parts.note: the I of I'll goes too, since the clue says I'll go

explanation.surface: Hamlet staged at London's Almeida theatre, minus a Holmesian villain, with a speaker agreeing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Almeida is a London theatre. Removing M and I from ALMEIDA leaves ALEDA, which 'produced by' rearranges; 'I'll go with that' says I also leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Aldea is the Spanish word for a village or small rural settlement, a hamlet.

clue.text: Composed cleverness that's heading off for disaster

indicators.note: a disaster leaves things in disarray, so the letters are rearranged
the heading, the first letter, of cleverness goes

explanation.surface: Cool cleverness that's heading for disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading off' drops C from CLEVERNESS; 'for disaster' rearranges ERVELNESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerveless can mean calm and unflustered, the cool of someone self-possessed.

clue.text: Apprehension as kaput English got beaten

indicators.note: being beaten knocks the letters out of shape

explanation.surface: Fear that the English side, done for, got beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Apprehension in the sense of grasp or comprehension; uptake is quickness of understanding.

clue.text: Wonderful place to keep ashes say?

indicators.note: say signals that a word spoken aloud is meant

parts.note: a fireplace grate holds the ashes of a fire

explanation.surface: Praise for a fine spot to keep a loved one's ashes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ashes' suggests an urn, but the fire grate is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Great is an informal synonym for excellent or marvellous.

clue.text: Would-be ruler before submission?

parts.note: pre is a prefix meaning before
a tender is a formal submission or bid

explanation.surface: A would-be king, before he has to bow down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Submission' suggests yielding, but it is a bid offered.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretender claims a throne he does not hold, like the Old Pretender.

clue.text: Take last couple of bits of rich cottage cheese

indicators.text: Take last couple of bits of
indicators.note: the last two letters of each of the words rich and cottage are taken away

explanation.surface: Instructions to cut the rind off a rich cottage cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take' means remove: drop CH from RICH and GE from COTTAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ricotta is a soft Italian whey cheese.

clue.text: Mean to make known how old you are

parts.note: to aver is to declare or state
your age is how old you are

explanation.surface: It's unkind to announce how old someone is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like a verb or 'unkind', but it is the statistical noun.
explanation.definitionFit: An average is the arithmetic mean of a set of values.

clue.text: Amazing person spreading new hope to enthral dissenters

indicators.note: to enthral is to hold captive, so one part holds the other
spreading scatters the letters into a new order

parts.note: no-men are those who say no, the opposite of yes-men

explanation.surface: An inspiring figure spreading hope that wins over even the doubters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spreading' turns N plus HOPE into PHEON, which holds NOMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A phenomenon can be a remarkable person, a prodigy.

clue.text: Slim tucked into pasties with seconds indicating quality of meat

indicators.note: one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: pasties are pies
slim means thin

explanation.surface: A slim person tucking into pasties and second helpings while judging the meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meat' is figurative: the substance of an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: Pithiness is concise substance, the meatiness of a forceful statement.

clue.text: The Northern French road is straight

parts.note: in northern English dialect 'the' is clipped to t'
rue is French for street

explanation.surface: A road in northern France runs dead straight.
explanation.definitionFit: True can mean exactly aligned, as in a wall that is true.

clue.text: Insect that infests crossing bitumen? It slows things down

indicators.note: the insect spans across the other word, holding it

parts.note: the red ant is an invasive pest species
tar is bitumen

explanation.surface: Ants crawling across a tarred road are slowed by the sticky surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A retardant is a substance that delays a process, as a fire retardant does.

clue.text: Media reporting of old fellow's anger?

parts.note: cove is a dated British word for a chap, with 's linking
rage is anger

explanation.surface: The press reports an old man's furious outburst.
explanation.definitionFit: Coverage is the reporting given to an event by newspapers and broadcasters.

clue.text: Time to make enquiries for a job

parts.note: to ask is to make enquiries

explanation.surface: A moment to ask around about vacancies.
explanation.definitionFit: A task is a piece of work to be done.

clue.text: Cut long story short, rough gist about bundle, it's stuck at top of windpipe

definitions.text: it's stuck at top of windpipe

indicators.note: cut, read with the trailing short, says the long story is trimmed at its end

parts.note: an epic is a long story; short echoes the cut, the familiar phrase 'cut a long story short'

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters surround the other piece
rough means knocked about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a lot is a bundle of goods at auction

explanation.surface: A rough summary of a long tale wrapped up quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rough' turns GIST into GTIS, which goes about LOT to give GLOTTIS.
explanation.definitionFit: This flap of cartilage sits above the larynx and closes the airway during swallowing.

clue.text: Skin from wee fish

parts.note: wee and pee are both informal words for urine
the ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Skinning a tiny fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wee' looks like 'small' in a Scottish sense; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Peeling as a noun is the skin stripped from fruit or vegetables.

clue.text: We hear one gets hot in the spring, old man

indicators.note: we hear signals a word that sounds like another

parts.words: one gets hot in the spring
parts.note: a geyser is a hot spring that erupts

explanation.surface: An old man gets hot under the collar in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' is a water source, not the season.
explanation.definitionFit: Geezer is British slang for a man, often an old one.

clue.text: Tree climbing enactment enthusiast

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means going up, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a law is an enactment of parliament
a nut is a keen enthusiast

explanation.surface: A keen tree-climber acting out a scene.
explanation.definitionFit: The walnut is a deciduous tree grown for nuts and timber.

clue.text: With no student initially able to read, say it again

indicators.note: with no says a piece is removed

parts.note: a literate person can read
L is a learner or student, as on L-plates; initially says it goes from the start

explanation.surface: Telling a pupil who can't yet read to repeat it.
explanation.definitionFit: To iterate is to repeat, to perform or utter again.

clue.text: Mathematician/engineer looking for regularity in equal gears

indicators.note: regularity signals taking letters at regular intervals, the odd ones

explanation.surface: An engineer checking equal gears for regular motion.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonhard Euler was the eighteenth-century Swiss mathematician who also worked on mechanics and engineering.

clue.text: This might be raised in surprise report of London's elite

definitions.text: This might be raised in surprise

indicators.note: a Cockney Londoner, dropping the h, would say the word so it sounds like this one

parts.note: highbrow means intellectually elite

explanation.surface: A report on London's high society prompts surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney speech drops initial h, so 'highbrow' comes out as 'eyebrow'.
explanation.definitionFit: People raise an eyebrow to show surprise or scepticism.

clue.text: It goes round back of elbow and back of foot

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter

parts.note: the heel is the back of the foot

explanation.surface: Something circling behind the elbow and the heel.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheel is a disc that rotates on an axle.

clue.text: Plant sprawling in tangle by base of tree

indicators.note: sprawling means spread untidily, so the letters are rearranged
the base, in an across clue, is the word's last letter

explanation.surface: A plant sprawling in a tangle at the foot of a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Eglantine is the sweetbriar, a wild rose.

clue.text: A Thousand Detained In Terror Alert!

indicators.note: the pieces are held inside another word

parts.note: awe is dread or reverential fear

explanation.surface: A headline: a thousand people held during a terror alert.
explanation.definitionFit: Alert and awake both mean watchful, fully conscious.

clue.text: Design that traps rodent say in animal pen

indicators.note: the pen traps the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs
the rat is a rodent
e.g. means for example, here signalled by say

explanation.surface: A plan for catching a rat in a pigsty.
explanation.definitionFit: A strategy is a plan or scheme of action.

clue.text: Sign of damage that's nearly entirely to do with teeth

parts.note: a dent is a sign of damage

indicators.note: nearly means one letter short of the full word

parts.note: all means entirely

explanation.surface: Damage that's almost all to do with teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Dental is the adjective relating to teeth.
